title: Scalable Vector Component Systems & Variants
subtitle: Nested Symbols, Button States, Responsive Layouts & Design Tokens

learningObjectives: Construct multi-variant UI component systems incorporating Primary, Secondary, Ghost, and Destructive button styles.
Architect hierarchical Nested Symbols (e.g. an icon symbol embedded within a button symbol) for compound updates.
Configure the Constraints Studio to establish responsive auto-resizing rules for cards and navigation bars.
Integrate Global Color Swatches as design tokens to enable instant thematic restyling across an entire component library.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: Building an enterprise design system requires more than isolated buttons; it requires an architectural ecosystem where changes cascade predictably. In Affinity Designer, this is achieved by combining three advanced vector engines: (1) Nested Symbols, where sub-components like icons or badges are symbols nested inside larger container symbols; (2) The Constraints Studio (View > Studio > Constraints), which defines responsive pinning rules (pin left, pin right, fixed width) so cards scale cleanly without distorting buttons or avatars; and (3) Global Color Swatches in the Swatches Studio, which act as native design tokens—re-tinting a single global swatch updates every component, border, and typography instance throughout the entire document.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity Designer 3.3.3 Constraints Engine, Nested Symbols & Global Swatches Specification

stepByStepInstructions.title: Create an Icon Sub-Symbol
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw a 16x16 px vector chevron icon (#FFFFFF). In the Symbols Studio, click 'Create' to register it as 'SubComponent_Icon_Chevron'.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Nest the Icon Inside a Master Button
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw a button container (160x44 px, 8px rounded corners, fill #4F46E5). Add an Artistic Text label ('Next Step'). Place an instance of your 'SubComponent_Icon_Chevron' inside the group. In the Symbols Studio, select the entire group and click 'Create' to register 'Component_Button_Action'. You have now created a Nested Symbol!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure Responsive Pinning in Constraints Studio
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Open View > Studio > Constraints. Select the chevron icon inside the button. In the Constraints panel, check 'Pin Right' and 'Fixed Width'. Select the text label and check 'Pin Left'. Drag the button's right edge wider: the chevron stays locked to the right margin while the button expands smoothly without distortion!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Define Global Swatches as Design Tokens
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: In the Swatches Studio, click the palette burger menu and select 'Add Global Color...'. Name it 'Token_Brand_Primary' and set value to #4F46E5. Apply this global swatch to your button fill. Notice the swatch thumbnail displays a distinct triangle badge indicating it is a live global token.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Test Cascade Architecture
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Duplicate your button component across 3 artboards. Double-click the 'Token_Brand_Primary' swatch in the Swatches Studio and change the hue to Purple (#7C3AED). Observe: Every button instance on every artboard updates color instantly. Then edit the original 'SubComponent_Icon_Chevron' to an arrow: Every button updates its icon automatically!

visualExamples.title: Constraints Studio Pinning Matrix
visualExamples.description: Standard pinning configurations for common UI components.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| UI Element | Pinning Configuration | Dimension Lock | Resize Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trailing Icon | Pin Right, Pin Center-Y | Fixed Width & Height | Stays docked to right edge with fixed icon size |
| Leading Logo | Pin Left, Pin Center-Y | Fixed Width & Height | Stays docked to left edge with fixed logo size |
| Card Body Copy | Pin Left, Pin Right, Pin Top | None | Stretches horizontally to fill card width |
| Modal Background | Pin Top, Bottom, Left, Right | None | Stretches responsively with parent artboard |

guidedPractice.title: Constructing an Adaptive Analytics Metric Card
guidedPractice.taskDescription: Build a responsive KPI card with nested metric pills, pinning rules, and global color tokens that resizes from 240px to 480px width flawlessly.
checkpoints: Create a nested symbol for a trend badge pill ('+24% Growth').

independentChallenge.title: Full-Spectrum Design System Library
independentChallenge.prompt: Construct a production-ready UI component kit in Affinity Designer: (1) Establish 4 global color tokens (Primary, Success, Warning, Neutral); (2) Build an Icon Sub-Symbol library (Arrow, Check, Close, Alert); (3) Build 4 Button Variants (Primary Filled, Secondary Outlined, Ghost, Destructive) using nested icon symbols and constraints; (4) Configure hover and disabled states with local overrides; (5) Archive the entire suite into the Assets Studio under 'Enterprise UI System' and export as 'Design_System_Tokens_v1.afassets'.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Neglecting to check 'Fixed Width' and 'Fixed Height' on icons inside responsive containers.
commonPitfalls.consequence: When the parent card or button is stretched wider, the circular or square icon stretches into a distorted oval.
commonPitfalls.solution: In the Constraints Studio, always lock 'Fixed Width' and 'Fixed Height' on icons, logos, and badges.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Using regular document swatches instead of Global Swatches for brand colors.
commonPitfalls.consequence: Updating a brand color requires manually selecting and re-tinting hundreds of individual vector paths.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always choose 'Add Global Color...' in the Swatches Studio menu. Global swatches display a distinctive corner triangle badge.

commonPitfalls.mistake: Nesting symbols more than 3 levels deep unnecessarily.
commonPitfalls.consequence: Creates confusion in the Layers Studio and increases mental overhead when troubleshooting override propagation.
commonPitfalls.solution: Keep nesting hierarchy disciplined: Design Tokens -> Sub-Symbols (Icons/Badges) -> Master Components (Buttons/Cards).

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary visual indicator that a color swatch in the Swatches Studio is a live Global Swatch?
options: It is marked with a padlock icon.
It displays a small white or gray triangle in its bottom-left corner.
It is outlined with a dotted red border.
It is sorted into a separate window.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Global Color Swatches in Affinity Designer are visually distinguished by a small triangle badge in their lower-left corner, signifying that edits to the swatch update all objects using that color.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which studio panel in Affinity Designer allows you to pin an icon to the right margin of a button so it does not distort when the button is resized wider?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The Constraints Studio (View > Studio > Constraints) allows you to define edge pinning (Pin Right) and dimension locking (Fixed Width) for responsive vector components.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens if you edit a Sub-Symbol (e.g. an icon) that is nested inside a Master Button Symbol?
options: The icon updates globally inside every button symbol instance that contains it.
The button symbol is automatically detached into a plain group.
The icon disappears from the canvas.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Nested Symbols exhibit compound inheritance: modifying the nested child symbol propagates changes through all parent master symbols that embed it.

keyTakeaways: Nested Symbols allow compound component architectures where sub-elements update seamlessly.
The Constraints Studio ensures responsive auto-resizing without distorting icons or margins.
Global Swatches function as design tokens, enabling instant document-wide theme re-coloration.
Combining Symbols, Assets, Constraints, and Global Tokens elevates Affinity Designer into an enterprise UI powerhouse.

slides.title: Architecting Enterprise Component Systems
slides.subtitle: Beyond Standalone Buttons to Scalable Systems
bullets: A true design system is an ecosystem of interdependent visual decisions.
Affinity Designer uniquely combines four powerful vector engines:
1. Nested Symbols: Compounds of symbols inside symbols.
2. Constraints Studio: Responsive pinning and dimension locking.
3. Global Swatches: Live color tokens that ripple through the whole document.
4. Assets Studio: Persistent global distribution across projects.
slides.proTip: This multi-engine synergy allows solo designers to manage enterprise-scale design systems.

slides.title: The Power of Nested Symbols
slides.subtitle: Compound Inheritance in Vector Architecture
bullets: Create an icon (e.g. chevron or arrow) and register it as an Icon Symbol.
Place instances of this icon symbol inside button and card Master Symbols.
Updating the icon symbol later propagates through all buttons, headers, and cards simultaneously.
Keeps your iconography 100% unified without touching individual parent components.
slides.proTip: Limit nesting depth to 2–3 levels for maximum clarity and maintainability.

slides.title: The Constraints Studio Architecture
slides.subtitle: Responsive Vector Auto-Resizing
bullets: Open via View > Studio > Constraints.
Edge Pinning: Pin Left, Right, Top, or Bottom relative to the parent container.
Dimension Locking: Fixed Width, Fixed Height, or maintain proportional aspect ratio.
Prevents icons, badges, and avatars from stretching when a card is widened for tablet or desktop.
slides.callout: Always lock 'Fixed Width' and 'Fixed Height' on circular avatars and icons!

slides.title: Pinning Rules for Common UI Elements
slides.subtitle: Standardizing Responsive Behaviors
bullets: Trailing Chevron: Pin Right, Pin Center-Y, Fixed Width, Fixed Height.
Leading Brand Logo: Pin Left, Pin Center-Y, Fixed Width, Fixed Height.
Card Body Description: Pin Left, Pin Right, Pin Top (stretches with card width).
Action Buttons in Dialog: Pin Right, Pin Bottom (docked to bottom-right corner).
slides.proTip: Test your constraints by selecting the parent container and dragging its corner handle.

slides.title: Global Color Swatches as Design Tokens
slides.subtitle: Document-Wide Thematic Color Control
bullets: In the Swatches Studio, select 'Add Global Color...' from the panel menu.
Global swatches display a distinct triangle badge in their lower-left corner.
Apply global swatches to component backgrounds, borders, and typography.
Editing the global swatch in the palette instantly repaints every instance document-wide!

slides.title: Building Multi-Variant Button Systems
slides.subtitle: Primary, Secondary, Ghost & Destructive
bullets: Primary: Solid brand fill (#4F46E5) with white label and icon.
Secondary: 1.5pt vector border with transparent fill and brand text.
Ghost: Transparent fill with subtle hover state tint.
Destructive: Coral red accent (#EF4444) for delete or danger actions.
All 4 variants utilize identical padding, corner radii, and nested icon symbols.
slides.proTip: Organize your button variants in a clean 4-column matrix on your design system canvas.
